_comment: Publisher-declared correction events, keyed by post id, oldest event first.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A content change cannot tell the exporter what KIND of change
it was. A correction of our own error and a note recording that the world has since
moved both rewrite the announcement text, and both move content_sha256. Deriving the class
from the bytes therefore writes 'factual_correction' onto a page whose note says, in
terms, that nothing we published was wrong - and factual_correction sticks.
So the kind is declared here rather than inferred, on the same footing as
scripts/approved-bylines.json: it is the publisher's decision about one specific
record and must not be second-guessed by a rule. This file is tracked, so
MANIFEST.sha256 and its signature cover it; the declaration is as tamper-evident as
the record it labels, and a third party can see what was declared and when.
A declared event governs classification.correction_class and, where a record has more
than one, classification.correction_history. It also forces correction_status to
'revised', because a declared event has by definition happened. factual_correction
still wins over any other class on the same record. A malformed entry is skipped
